question: In question E-003355/20251, the Commission was asked to provide information on the state of play regarding the examination of complaint CPLT(2024)00230, on the compatibility of the ‘Loi Descrozaille’ (EGalim III) with EU law and on the exchanges with the French authorities.

However, in its reply of 29 October 2025, the Commission merely stated that it was at that time still examining the complaint, and referred to complex legal issues and an ongoing dialogue since the beginning of 2023, without addressing the specific points of the original question. Market players are now reporting significant economic impacts and increasing market foreclosure, and are considering legal action.

Given the potential disruptions to the internal market, the question arises as to how the Commission, as guardian of the Treaties, views this development and what steps it is taking to ensure compliance with EU law. Therefore, the following clarifications are requested: 1.
What steps in the examination of complaint CPLT(2024)00230 have been completed since December 2023 and which are still pending?
Which of the ‘complex legal issues’ mentioned by the Commission are at the heart of the analysis and which provisions of EU law might be affected according to the assessment so far?
What is the concrete content and focus of the dialogue with the French authorities since 2023 and when is the examination of the complaint expected to be completed?
Supporters2
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.2.2026) The written question concerns a pending complaint which is the subject of exchanges with the Member State concerned in the on-going investigation. Disclosure of details of this investigation would affect the climate of mutual trust between the authorities of the Member State and the Commission.

The different services involved have conducted a detailed legal analysis of the relevant provisions of EGalim laws under EU law, particularly those imposing French law and jurisdiction on operators established in other Member States conducting pan-European negotiations and concluding contracts for the benefit of retailers active in different Member States, as soon as some of the products are sold in France.
The Commission is also following pending cases before the French national courts where the complainants request the courts to ask for preliminary rulings by the Court of Justice of the EU.

The Commission services are examining EGalim laws’ compatibility with the fundamental freedoms (freedom to provide services and freedom of establishment) and other EU legal instruments (Regulations (EC) No 593/2008 (Rome I), (EC) No 864/2007 (Rome II) and (EU) No 1215/2012)1.
